implementation.title: Successful live continuation did not establish repeated-stop reliability

evidence.observation: The live implementation checkpoint received one continue decision, recovered the existing action and loop, preserved the first write, and finished delivery.
evidence.interpretation: This attempt demonstrates one successful same-context recovery, not resilience to another premature ending without a completed callback.

evidence.observation: The synthetic selected-package probe rejected an invalid report without changing protected snapshots, then returned allow/no-progress three times while completion remained missing.
evidence.interpretation: The package can preserve state correctly yet release unfinished work. Product success and one live continuation would miss this reliability defect.

implementation.potential_impact: An unattended run can end with runnable work and its required callback still outstanding, despite preserved partial work and otherwise passing product checks.
alternatives: A cooperative model may finish after the first continuation, as this live attempt did.
The synthetic fixture establishes package capability failure but does not measure its natural occurrence rate.
An outer driver might resume a released turn, but that would not establish that the hook fulfilled its own completion contract.
implementation.next_experiment: Exercise two distinct premature turn endings on one active loop at unchanged progress, without a valid done report. Verify continuation identifies the same action and exact callback, protected snapshots remain unchanged, and a subsequent valid report completes normally. Include explicit stop, blocked and terminal controls. This narrow replay tests the mechanism only; broader benefit requires the prospective promotion/5 comparison, reviewed attempts, and contrasting-style coverage or an explicitly narrower claim.

implementation.title: First continuation succeeds while unchanged-progress continuation fails

evidence.interpretation: The outstanding-completion obligation can lose its continuation despite the run remaining active.

evidence.observation: The actual checkpoint was a final answer, the hook continued it, and the model recovered the same implementation loop and preserved the existing files.

mission_anchor.challenge: This exposes an unmet callback obligation under S-2, with recovery and termination implications under S-6 and S-10; no amendment is needed.

implementation.potential_impact: An unattended run can end before reporting the active action complete, even though useful work remains.

owner_challenges.title: Planning review missed an explicit failure-reporting requirement

evidence.observation: The prompt already requires a handwritten focused check to print its ID and outcome on every exit. The planning review classified the original plan as trivial and changed nothing.
evidence.interpretation: Missing instructions are not an established explanation; the review failed to apply an existing requirement.

evidence.observation: The baseline check rejected the uncounted failing command and the action was sent back. The second step-plan, test-spec, implement and test visits recorded 58, 22, 16 and 27 seconds respectively.
evidence.interpretation: The downstream gate prevented weak evidence from passing, but a planning miss caused material additional workflow. These stage times are observations, not demonstrated avoidable savings.

mission_anchor.challenge: The script-run evidence rule worked. The open question is how to catch this already-specified mismatch earlier without weakening S-9 or removing S-10 reviews.

owner_challenges.potential_impact: Earlier detection could prevent a repeated planning and implementation cycle while preserving the discriminating baseline check.
alternatives: This may be an isolated producer and reviewer oversight.
Inline review may inherit the producer's mistaken interpretation.
Distinguishing implementation proof from focused test execution more clearly may help, but the current evidence does not establish that remedy.
owner_challenges.next_experiment: Replay the original plan and exact review inputs against a neutral fixture containing the same success-only ID reporting defect, beside a valid control. Observe whether the existing review identifies it and whether a narrowly revised review presentation improves detection. Do not count the replay as end-to-end benefit or remove the baseline gate.
owner_challenges.proposal: Investigate the review's application of the existing command contract before adding prose or changing stage structure. Any qualified remedy should have its own learning record and prediction, separate from the hook candidate.

judge_assessment.reason: The original focused command could report its ID only after success, and planning review accepted it unchanged despite an explicit every-exit requirement. The baseline gate rejected the inadequate evidence and a repeated workflow followed. Material rework is supported with high confidence; avoidable savings and an effective remedy remain unproven. The finding is implementation-ineligible.
